newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INTERVIEW - Sarawak eyes high-tech role in Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Sarawak eyes high-tech role in Malaysia.

text.p: Malaysia's Borneo state of Sarawak is wooing electronics firms to help transform the sparsely populated forested territory into an industrial powerhouse, its Industrial Development Minister said.

Sarawak plans to set up an investment zone for world-class information technology companies along the lines of peninsula Malaysia's Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC), Abang Johari Abang Openg told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday.

The state, as large as peninsula Malaysia itself, is actively encouraging electronics plants in northern Penang state, dubbed Malaysia's Silicon Valley, to expand operations to Sarawak where land is plentiful.
The moves are part of Sarawak's "bid to become a fully industrialised state", Abang Johari said.
"We are going for high-tech automation...where you don't need a lot of labour. That is, the upper end of industry."

The manufacturing sector's contribution to Sarawak's gross domestic product (GDP) jumped from 6.5 percent in 1981 to 20.4 percent last year. It is projected to contribute 28 percent in the year 2000, he said.
Government figures showed that Sarawak's GDP expanded by 13.5 percent in 1995, much higher than Malaysia's 9.6 percent. Figures for 1996 were not available.
To keep up the brisk economic pace, the Sarawak government has launched more ambitious plans.
Abang Johari met officials of state telecommunications firm, Telekom Malaysia Bhd earlier this week to discuss how Sarawak could be plugged into the information superhighway.

The Multimedia Super Corridor, a brainchild of Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, covers some 700 square kilometres between the capital of Kuala Lumpur and a new international airport under construction.
Sarawak is calling its own corridor "the Mini MSC". It will be located at the Demak Industrial Estate in Kota Samarahan, just outside the state capital of Kuching.
The state government said recently the Mini MSC may well be ready in the next five years and will help Sarawakians to leap frog into the next century.
"Our infrastructure must be there to enable the application of information technology to be used by the industries, MNCs (multinational corporations). This is very important for us.

"We are not rivalling Penang. We have been working very closely with Penang Development Corporation and what we do is we complement the industry in Penang by encouraging them to have their expansion plans in Sarawak. Penang has land constraints," Abang Johari said.

Sarawak's Chief Minister Abdul Taib Mahmud on Wednesday announced a plan to develop a 100-150 acre industrial park near a key border crossing with Indonesia's Kalimantan state for labour-intensive industries.
The project will add to a slate of mega projects in the state, led by the 13 billion ringgit ($5.26 billion) Bakun hydro-electric dam.

Other projects are mainly concentrated in the town of Bintulu, including a 20 billion ringgit industrial park, a two billion ringgit paper and pulp factory, and a two billion ringgit aluminium smelting plant.
